request_context: A request to write up a formal program-level decision document that compares options, weighs trade-offs and recommends a course of action for stakeholders.

rules.source_quote: Include a "do nothing" option as baseline.
rules.outcome: Among the options compared is an explicit option of taking no action or keeping the current state, analysed like the others and serving as the baseline for comparison.
rules.why: Without a status-quo baseline, readers cannot judge whether any change is worth its cost and risk.
rules.scenario_hint: Request to document a decision between two or more proposed changes to a program.

rules.outcome: The weights given to the evaluation criteria add up to exactly the whole (all of the importance), and the arithmetic is consistent.
rules.why: Weights that do not add up distort the weighted totals and undermine the ranking.
rules.scenario_hint: Request for a scored comparison of options against weighted criteria such as cost, time and risk.

rules.source_quote: Score each option per criterion (1-5). Calculate weighted score.
rules.outcome: Each option is scored on every criterion using a small fixed numeric scale, and a weighted total per option is calculated and shown so the ranking can be verified.
rules.why: Unscored or uncalculated comparisons are subjective and cannot be checked.
rules.scenario_hint: Request to compare several options quantitatively before a recommendation.

rules.source_quote: Recommendation contradicts evaluation matrix without stated rationale
rules.outcome: The recommended option is the one with the highest weighted score, or, if it differs, the answer explicitly states the overriding factors that justify departing from the scores.
rules.why: A recommendation that silently contradicts its own analysis destroys trust in the document.
rules.scenario_hint: Request where a qualitatively appealing option scores lower than another in the analysis.

rules.source_quote: what happens if no decision is made (default outcome)
rules.outcome: The background states what will happen by default if no decision is taken, along with why the decision is needed now and the constraints such as budget, timeline or compliance.
rules.why: Without the cost of inaction and the trigger, urgency and constraints are unclear to decision makers.
rules.scenario_hint: Request to document a decision that has a deadline or a trigger event.

rules.source_quote: Each option has: description, pros, cons, effort estimate (T-shirt size), risk level
rules.outcome: Every option has a description, both advantages and disadvantages, a rough effort size (small to large) and a risk rating, with none left blank for any option.
rules.why: Missing pros, cons, effort or risk for an option makes the comparison lopsided.
rules.scenario_hint: Request to lay out several candidate approaches with their trade-offs.

rules.outcome: The document analyses a manageable number of alternatives, at least two and no more than five, rather than a single option or a sprawling list.
rules.why: One option is not a decision, and too many options dilute the analysis.
rules.scenario_hint: Request where many possible approaches exist and must be narrowed for decision makers.

rules.source_quote: revisit conditions (what would trigger reconsideration), and expiry date (when to review regardless)
rules.outcome: The record states what circumstances would trigger reconsidering the decision and a date by which it will be reviewed regardless.
rules.why: Decisions made under assumptions go stale if there is no trigger or date for revisiting them.
rules.scenario_hint: Request to record a decision that rests on assumptions likely to change.

rules.source_quote: Decision record missing decision maker or date
rules.outcome: The decision record names who made the decision and the date, together with the option selected and its rationale, and notes any dissenting views.
rules.why: An unattributed, undated decision cannot be audited or relied on later.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to document a decision that has been made.

rules.outcome: Stakeholders are identified by role: who decides, who is consulted, who is informed, and who drives the process.
rules.why: Unclear ownership leaves it ambiguous who may decide and who must be heard.
rules.scenario_hint: Request for a decision document involving several teams or leaders.

rules.source_quote: **Decision Title & Status** — Draft / Under Review / Decided / Superseded
rules.outcome: The document opens with a title and a current status showing whether it is a draft, under review, decided or replaced.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to produce a formal program decision document.

rules.source_quote: Options Table** — columns: Option, Description, Pros, Cons, Effort, Risk
rules.outcome: Options are shown in a table with a row per option and columns for description, advantages, disadvantages, effort and risk, followed by a separate scoring table with totals.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to produce a formal program decision document.
